hero_kpi_rationale: The Savings and Impact KPI is the Hero because it represents savings achieved by the company through its Performance Chemicals restructuring initiatives, reaching $105M since November 2023, which is a key driver of its strategic transformation.

kpis.name: Savings and Impact
kpis.explanation: Savings realized through Performance Chemicals restructuring initiatives
kpis.description: The PC Repositioning Actions restructuring initiatives enabled the company to realize approximately $105 million in cash savings since November 2023, distributed between cost of sales (75%), general and administrative expenses (20%), and research expenses (5%).

kpis.name: Long Lived Asset Impairment Charge
kpis.explanation: Impairment charge on long-lived assets of the Road Markings group from Performance Chemicals
kpis.description: Following due diligence for the potential sale of the Road Markings asset group in Q4 2025, a non-cash impairment charge of $109.3 million was recorded, allocated between property, plant and equipment ($25.2M) and intangible assets ($84.1M).
kpis.signal: Significant impairment charge related to strategic asset evaluation

kpis.name: Performance Chemicals Repositioning Total Charges
kpis.explanation: Total charges expected for Performance Chemicals restructuring initiatives
kpis.description: The Performance Chemicals repositioning program is expected to generate approximately $370 million in total charges, composed of $255M in non-cash charges related to assets and $115M in cash charges ($25M in personnel costs and $90M in other restructuring costs).

kpis.name: Goodwill Impairment Charge - Advanced Polymer Technologies
kpis.explanation: Full goodwill impairment charge for the Advanced Polymer Technologies division
kpis.description: In Q2 2025, following escalation of international trade tensions and consumer uncertainty, a non-cash impairment charge of $183.8 million was recorded for the Advanced Polymer Technologies reporting unit, representing the entirety of associated goodwill.
kpis.signal: Significant goodwill impairment due to industrial demand contraction

risks.title: Dependence on third parties for critical services
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned first among critical operations, with strong language on possible interruptions, high costs, and direct impacts on production. Dependence on third parties for essential services such as water, energy, or wastewater treatment at Covington and Warrington is recurring and exacerbated by shared financial responsibilities. The Industrial category carries high weighting in case of failure. This risk is stable compared to the prior year.

risks.title: Supply chain disruptions
risks.score_rationale: The factor is well-developed with specific examples (lignin, TOFA) and recurring threats such as port strikes or cost increases. Language indicates a frequent and tangible risk. While the Supply Chain category is less weighted than an existential risk, direct operational impact justifies high severity. Mentioned similarly to the prior year.

risks.title: Risk on products manufactured at a single site
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly highlights that certain key products (extruded honey, caprolactone, etc.) are manufactured at only a single site. Loss of one site would result in total interruption for these products. Language is alarming ('only made at a single site', 'limited ability to shift'). This risk is critical because it combines geographic concentration and lack of redundancy. It is stable compared to N-1.

risks.title: Technology competition in vehicles
risks.score_rationale: The passage on electric vehicles and sealed tanks is detailed and highlights an existential threat to the Performance Materials segment. The text clearly indicates that the decline in internal combustion engines reduces demand for activated carbon. Language is concerning ('reduce demand', 'financial results could be negatively impacted'). Technology transition is accelerated by regulation. This risk is increasing compared to N-1.

risks.title: Risks related to international operations
risks.score_rationale: The risk covers numerous factors (exchange rates, geopolitics, taxes, pandemics) and represents 43% of sales. Language is cautious but repeated, with concrete threats such as wars in Ukraine and the Middle East. The Geopolitical category is moderately weighted, but the magnitude of risk justifies high severity. Mention similar to the prior year.

risks.title: Union tensions and strikes
risks.score_rationale: The document mentions multiple collective agreements under renegotiation, particularly at Covington. While relations are described as positive, the risk of strikes or disruption is explicit. Language is cautious but real ('no guarantee', 'work stoppages'). The Key Person category is moderately weighted, but potential operational impact is high. This risk is stable compared to N-1.

risks.title: Dependence on government spending for roads
risks.score_rationale: The pavement technologies segment depends heavily on government budgets for infrastructure. The text emphasizes funding delays, budget cuts, and political changes as threats. Language is repeated and stresses indirect but significant dependence. The Macro category is moderately weighted, but sector exposure is strong. This risk is stable compared to N-1.
